newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Shining Path attacks Ashaninka indians.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Shining Path attacks Ashaninka indians.

text.p: At least 100 guerrillas from Peru's Maoist Shining Path movement attacked three remote Ashaninka Indian villages this week, killing or kidnapping an unknown number of natives, anti-terrorist police sources said Friday.
They said the rebel column stormed the communities of Matireni, Shimapango and Chikireni in the River Ene region of Peru's central jungle early on Monday. News of the attack reached Lima on Friday.

"There were at least 100 rebels who went into the villages, although there may have been more outside," one source said. "They executed some Indians who were giving information to the security forces, and took others away with them."
Around 5,000 Ashaninkas, from an estimated total of 30,000 to 40,000 in the tribe, have died at the hands of Shining Path since the rebels first entered the zone in 1986.

Although their presence in the area has been weakened in recent years, Shining Path's military leader Oscar Ramirez Durand, alias "Comrade Feliciano," still hides out in the Ene River valley. Several hundred armed guerrillas move relatively freely around the jungle, the sources said.
